question: Intestinal juice converts protein in food into which molecules?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Amino acid**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Intestinal juice converts protein in food into amino acids
 
• The small intestine breaks down proteins into amino acids, carbohydrates into glucose, and fats into fatty acids and glycerol.
 
• The enzymes in intestinal juice, such as erepsin or peptidases, help break down proteins into amino acids.
 
• The stomach breaks down proteins into smaller chains of amino acids using hydrochloric acid and proteases.
 
• These smaller chains then move into the small intestine.
 
• After digestion, nutrients are absorbed in the form of amino acids, glucose, fatty acids, and glycerol.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Glycerol
 
 
• Glycerol is a key component of triglycerides and phospholipids, which are essential for energy storage and cell membrane structure.
 
• Glycerol has various industrial applications, including in the production of cosmetics, pharmaceuticals, and food additives.
 
 
 
• Fatty Acids
 
 
• Fatty acids are the primary components of triglycerides, which serve as a long-term energy storage form in the body.
 
• Fatty acids are essential for the formation of cell membranes, providing a barrier between the cell and its environment.
 
 
 
• Glucose
 
 
• Glucose is the primary source of energy for cells, fueling cellular processes like metabolism and muscle contraction.
 
 
• Glucose is the basic unit of carbohydrates, which are essential for energy storage and structural support in organisms.
